headline: Congress extended a temporary federal order that keeps fentanyl-related substances in the strictest drug category until October 22, 2021.
what_it_does: The Drug Enforcement Administration had placed fentanyl-related substances in Schedule I of the Controlled Substances Act on a temporary basis. That order was set to expire on May 6, 2021. This law extends the order until October 22, 2021, so the substances stay in Schedule I during that time.

who_it_affects.group: People who make, possess, or distribute fentanyl-related substances
who_it_affects.how: They stay subject to Schedule I rules, which carry federal penalties for illegal manufacturing, possession, and distribution, for the extended period.

who_it_affects.group: Researchers and laboratories that handle these substances
who_it_affects.how: They remain under Schedule I controls, which generally limit lawful handling to those with the required federal registration.
They can continue to use Schedule I classification when charging offenses involving these substances until the extended order ends.

when_it_takes_effect: The extension took effect when the law was enacted on May 4, 2021, before the original order expired on May 6, 2021, and it runs until October 22, 2021.
